title: The Miser and the Loaves of Bread
summary: The Fifth Vizier recounted the story of an affluent grain merchant of Baghdad named Abu Bakr, whose greed was an affliction to his soul:
keywords: the miser and the loaves of bread
full_text:
The Fifth Vizier recounted the story of an affluent grain merchant of Baghdad named Abu Bakr, whose greed was an affliction to his soul:

'Abu Bakr lived in a grand mansion, but he was so terrified of poverty that he ate only bitter radishes and stale crusts, locking his fine wheat loaves in heavy iron-bound cupboards. Whenever his wife asked for flour to bake fresh bread for their children, he would moan: "Famine is coming! We must hoard every crumb, or we shall perish in the streets!"

One winter, a severe frost swept over the city, and a poor widow knocked at his door, weeping: "O merchant, my children are shivering and have not tasted bread for two days; sell me a single loaf on credit!"

Abu Bakr drove her away with harsh insults, slammed his heavy door, and went into his storeroom to gloat over fifty loaves of fine white bread he had hoarded in his cedar chest.

When he unlocked the chest, a dreadful sight met his eyes: because he had kept the chest sealed without air or sunlight, green mold had covered every single loaf, and a family of mice had devoured the interior, leaving only bitter dust!

At that moment, from the cottage next door, came the joyful sounds of singing. His neighbor, an honest baker who shared half his daily loaves with the poor, was enjoying a warm supper with his healthy family.

Abu Bakr sat among his moldy crusts, weeping in bitter realization that hoarded wealth turns to rot, while bread shared in love feeds both the body and the soul forever.'
moral: He who hoards bread in fear of hunger turns his sustenance into dust; sharing brings true abundance.
